narr: A slow-moving frontal boundary brought several rounds of showers and thunderstorms to central Illinois from November 3rd through 5th. Storm total rainfall during that time ranged from 2 to 4 inches, with a few locations across the Illinois River Valley picking up greater than 4 inches. Due to antecedent drought conditions through September and October, much of the heavy rainfall readily soaked into the ground and caused little issue other than standing water in urban locations. Localized flash flooding occurred under a viaduct in Champaign likely due to storm drains clogged with leaves and other debris.
ev: A vehicle stalled in high water beneath a viaduct in Champaign.
lsr: Viaduct flooding relayed by broadcast media from University of IL police with a car stalled out.
